doc.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

chapter: Childhood in China and move to Japan
title: Leaving China for Japan after the war
summary: She moved to Japan at 15 after the war ended and her father lost everything.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: That’s an interesting way, a good analogy. I understand you were born in China and you moved to Japan — you were about 17 is that right?
Can I ask why your family moved, and that particular—
Yeah, that was a very important time for both of those countries.

Yes. I think I was lucky, the fact that I was very little. I think my parents, it was such a terrible blow, especially for my father because, almost he built his business in China, that’s why he wanted to remain, that’s where he wanted to finish his life. Then the war was ended and he lost everything and it was something that he totally didn’t expect. I think it was very difficult for him.
